title: Unitary Representations Positive Type and Gns

items.title: Strongly continuous unitary representation, invariance and intertwiners
items.statement: For a topological group G and complex Hilbert space H, a unitary representation is a homomorphism G→U(H), where U(H) consists of bijective complex-linear isometries, such that g→π(g)v is norm-continuous for every v. A closed subspace is invariant when π(g)M=M for every g; irreducible means H≠0 and only 0,H are closed invariant subspaces. A bounded intertwiner T satisfies Tπ(g)=ρ(g)T; equivalence uses a unitary intertwiner. The commutant is the algebra of bounded self-intertwiners.
items.strategy: Define all terms with the inherited first-variable-linear Hilbert pairing. The equality π(g)M=M follows from invariance under all g and g inverse. Prove from the group law and unitarity that continuity at the identity for each vector is equivalent to continuity at every group element. A bounded intertwiner has a well-defined adjoint when Countable Choice is later assumed, but the definition itself is choice-free.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C
Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups, corrected 2025 notes, §3.4

items.axiom_audit: choice-free

items.title: Continuity criteria for unitary representations
items.statement: Let G be a topological group and π:G→U(H) a group homomorphism. The following conditions are equivalent: π is strongly continuous; every matrix coefficient is continuous; and, for each total subset S⊆H, every diagonal coefficient g↦⟨π(g)v,v⟩ with v∈S is continuous at the identity. Here S is total when every x∈H can be approximated in norm by finite complex linear combinations of elements of S.
items.strategy: For strongly continuous π, use the preceding coefficient-continuity result. Conversely, if diagonal coefficients are continuous at e on a total S, put q_v(g)=⟨π(g)v,v⟩ and r=||v||². The first-linear inner-product expansion gives ||π(g)v−v||²=−(z+z̄), where z=q_v(g)−r. This is nonnegative and at most 2|z| by the complex modulus triangle inequality and |z̄|=|z|. Complex-metric continuity makes it tend to zero, so diagonal orbit maps are continuous at e, including v=0. Linearity and the norm triangle inequality extend this to span S; density and ||π(g)x−x||≤2||x−w||+||π(g)w−w|| extend it to H. Group translations move continuity at e to every g. The same reverse argument with S=H handles continuity of all coefficients. Define totality by the norm approximation property; the empty total subset case forces H=0 and is covered by the estimate. No polarization or choice is used.

references.title: Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups, corrected 2025 notes, §3.4
Neeb, An Introduction to Unitary Representations of Lie Groups, §§3.4, 4.2 and 5.3

items.title: Cyclic vector and cyclic unitary representation
items.statement: A vector ξ in a unitary representation (π,H) is cyclic if the complex linear span of {π(g)ξ:g∈G} is dense in H; the representation is cyclic if it has such a vector, including the zero-space convention used for the zero positive-type function.
items.strategy: Define the algebraic orbit span before its norm closure. The zero representation is allowed as a cyclic realization with ξ=0, but irreducibility always requires H nonzero. This convention keeps the zero positive-type function in the unnormalized GNS theorem and out of the normalized statement.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C
Bekka and de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B

items.title: Schur lemma for complex unitary representations
items.statement: Assume AC. For nonzero irreducible complex unitary representations π,ρ, every bounded self-intertwiner of π is scalar. A nonzero bounded intertwiner π→ρ exists only when π and ρ are unitarily equivalent; consequently inequivalent irreducibles have no nonzero bounded intertwiner.
items.strategy: The adjoint of an intertwiner is an intertwiner because π(g) and ρ(g) are unitary. Split a self-intertwiner into two bounded self-adjoint commuting parts. For a nonscalar self-adjoint A, its spectrum has at least two points: a singleton spectrum makes A scalar by the continuous calculus. Choose disjoint nonempty relatively open spectral sets U,V. Spectral support gives E_A(U),E_A(V) nonzero; orthogonality makes E_A(U) proper. The Borel commutant clause makes E_A(U) commute with all π(g), giving a forbidden closed invariant range. Thus each self-adjoint part is scalar. For T:π→ρ nonzero, T*T=cI with c>0, so c^(-1/2)T is an isometry with closed nonzero invariant range, hence onto by irreducibility of ρ. This avoids the false singleton-projection inference in BHV A.2.2.

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC because the published Borel functional calculus and spectral-support theorem assume it; the specific use is the nontrivial commuting spectral projection.

items.title: Matrix coefficient of a unitary representation
items.statement: For any group homomorphism π:G→U(H) and ξ,η∈H, define c_{ξ,η}(g)=⟨π(g)ξ,η⟩, with the Hilbert pairing linear in the first variable. If G is topological and π is strongly continuous, then c_{ξ,η} is continuous.
items.strategy: Define coefficients for algebraic unitary homomorphisms without assuming continuity. Under the additional hypothesis of strong continuity, prove continuity pointwise by orbit continuity, Cauchy–Schwarz, and the complex metric d_C(z,w)=|z−w|; later bounds and uniform continuity are separate.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C
Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups, corrected 2025 notes, §3.4

items.axiom_audit: choice-free

items.title: Bounds and two-sided uniform continuity of unitary coefficients
items.statement: For a strongly continuous unitary representation, every coefficient c_{ξ,η} satisfies |c_{ξ,η}(g)|≤||ξ||·||η|| and is both left and right uniformly continuous on G in the group uniformities.
items.strategy: First prove locally that any complex-linear norm isometry U preserves the inner product: the identities ||u+v||²−||u−v||²=4 Re⟨u,v⟩ and ||u+iv||²−||u−iv||²=4 Im⟨u,v⟩ recover both parts, and U preserves the four norms. Cauchy–Schwarz and isometry give |c(g)|≤||ξ||||η||. For the repository's left uniformity, whose basic entourage is x⁻¹y∈U, put y=xh; then |c(y)−c(x)|≤||π(h)ξ−ξ||||η|| uniformly in x. For the right uniformity, whose basic entourage is yx⁻¹∈U, put y=hx; inner-product preservation gives |c(y)−c(x)|≤||ξ||||π(h⁻¹)η−η|| uniformly in x. Strong continuity at e controls the first difference; strong continuity for η and continuity of inversion control the second. Translate these bounds into the epsilon-entourage definition of uniform continuity with the usual metric uniformity on C. Handle zero vectors directly; no commutativity, local compactness, Haar measure, or choice is used.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C
Neeb, An Introduction to Unitary Representations of Lie Groups, §§3.4, 4.2 and 5.3

items.title: Continuous positive-type function and normalized positive-type cone
items.statement: A continuous φ:G→C has positive type when for every n≥1, possibly repeated g_1,…,g_n∈G and arbitrary c_1,…,c_n∈C, the Hermitian matrix (φ(g_i^{-1}g_j)) is positive semidefinite, including zero coefficients. Write P(G) for this cone, P_1(G)={φ∈P(G):φ(e)=1}, and 0≤ψ≤φ when ψ and φ−ψ lie in P(G).
items.strategy: The n=1 case gives φ(e)≥0. The n=2 cases at e,g yield φ(g^{-1})=conj φ(g) and |φ(g)|≤φ(e), so φ(e)=0 forces φ=0. These finite-matrix consequences will be proved inline in the definition or in the immediately following form lemma; do not restrict to distinct group elements or to nonzero test scalars.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C
Neeb, An Introduction to Unitary Representations of Lie Groups, §§3.4, 4.2 and 5.3
Bekka and de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B

items.title: Diagonal unitary coefficients have positive type
items.statement: For any strongly continuous unitary representation (π,H) and ξ∈H, φ(g)=⟨π(g)ξ,ξ⟩ has positive type and φ(e)=||ξ||².
items.strategy: First derive that each complex-linear norm isometry U preserves the inner product: expand the squared norms of x±y and x±iy, and recover the real and imaginary parts. For a finite list g_i put v_i=π(g_i)ξ; unitarity and the homomorphism law give φ(g_i^{-1}g_j)=⟨v_j,v_i⟩. The standard positive-semidefinite quadratic form of this matrix is ||Σ_j c_jv_j||²≥0, including repeats and zero coefficients. Continuity follows from the matrix-coefficient definition under strong continuity. At e use π(e)=I; ξ=0 gives the zero positive-type function. No choice is used.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C
Bekka and de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B

items.axiom_audit: choice-free

items.title: Positive-type functions define the GNS pre-Hilbert form
items.statement: For a continuous positive-type φ on any topological group, the finitely supported complex functions C^(G) carry the positive semidefinite first-linear sesquilinear form B_φ(f,h)=Σ_{x,y}f(x)conj(h(y))φ(y^{-1}x). Its null vectors are orthogonal to all vectors, so B_φ descends to an inner product after quotienting by the null space.
items.strategy: All sums are finite. The finite-matrix condition gives nonnegative diagonals; its two-point consequences give conjugate symmetry. Derive the semidefinite Cauchy–Schwarz inequality by positivity of B(f+zh,f+zh) for all complex z, including B(h,h)=0. It implies B(f,h)=0 for every h when B(f,f)=0, making the quotient pairing independent of representatives and positive definite. In particular B(δ_x,δ_y)=φ(y^{-1}x), with no Haar measure and no choice.

references.title: Bekka and de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B
Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C

items.axiom_audit: choice-free

items.title: The GNS null space is invariant under left translation
items.statement: For the GNS form B_φ, the null set N={f:B_φ(f,f)=0} is a complex linear subspace, and every left translation L_g f(x)=f(g^{-1}x) carries N onto N. Thus L_g acts well-definedly on C^(G)/N.
items.strategy: Semidefinite Cauchy–Schwarz makes N the radical and therefore a linear subspace. Substitute x=gu,y=gv into the finite sum to obtain B_φ(L_g f,L_g h)=B_φ(f,h), because (gy)^{-1}(gx)=y^{-1}x. Both L_g and L_{g^{-1}} preserve N; they descend as inverse maps on the quotient. No measure or choice is needed.

references.title: Bekka and de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B
Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C

items.axiom_audit: choice-free

items.title: The GNS translation action is unitary and strongly continuous
items.statement: Let G be a topological group, let φ:G→C be continuous positive type, and let H_φ be the Hilbert completion of Q_φ=C^(G)/N_φ for the GNS form. Assume AC. Left translations induce maps on Q_φ that extend uniquely to π_φ(g)∈U(H_φ); the extensions satisfy π_φ(g)π_φ(h)=π_φ(gh), π_φ(e)=I, and every orbit g→π_φ(g)v is norm-continuous.
items.strategy: For T_g[f]=[L_gf], first verify B_φ(L_gf,L_gh)=B_φ(f,h) by finite reindexing, so the quotient map is an isometry and the null-space supplier makes it well-defined. AC implies Countable Choice, the premise of both the Hilbert-completion theorem and the unique bounded-map extension theorem; extend each T_g and use dense-set uniqueness for inverses and the group law. For [δ_x], the squared displacement is 2φ(e)−φ(x^{-1}gx)−φ((x^{-1}gx)^{-1}); continuity of φ and the conjugation maps makes it tend to zero, with an explicit nonnegative epsilon estimate. Triangle inequalities give continuity on finite spans; density and the uniform isometry bound 2||v−w|| extend it to the completion. Translate continuity from e to every g. Handle φ=0 as the zero Hilbert space. No other choice is used.

references.title: Bekka and de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B
Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C
Neeb, An Introduction to Unitary Representations of Lie Groups, §§3.4, 4.2 and 5.3

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC only to infer Countable Choice and apply the Hilbert-completion theorem and bounded-map extension theorem, both of which explicitly assume Countable Choice. The unique extensions require no additional choice; the finite reindexing and continuity estimates are choice-free.

items.title: GNS construction for a continuous positive-type function
items.statement: Assume AC. For a continuous positive-type function φ on a topological group G, the Hilbert completion of the null quotient of its GNS form carries a cyclic strongly continuous unitary representation π_φ and canonical vector ξ_φ=κ_φ([δ_e]) such that φ(g)=⟨π_φ(g)ξ_φ,ξ_φ⟩ and ||ξ_φ||²=φ(e). If φ=0, the Hilbert space and cyclic vector are zero.
items.strategy: Use the supplied completion map κ_φ and set ξ_φ=κ_φ([δ_e]). Left translation sends δ_e to δ_g, so the orbit maps to all point-mass classes; these span the quotient and are dense after completion. The point-mass form formula gives the coefficient and norm identities. If φ(e)=0, δ_e is null and the radical property gives B_φ(δ_e,δ_g)=φ(g^{-1})=0 for every g, hence φ=0; then the quotient and completion are zero and the cyclic convention covers the zero representation. AC is used only through Countable Choice in the completion and bounded-extension inputs to the translation-action lemma.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Theorem C.4.10 (GNS Construction)
references.locator: Appendix C §C.4, theorem and complete proof, printed pp. 376–377

references.title: Bachir Bekka and Pierre de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC only to infer Countable Choice and apply the Hilbert completion and unique bounded-extension inputs of the translation-action lemma. The specified point masses, finite spans, coefficient identities and zero-case proof use no further choice.

items.title: Uniqueness of the pointed cyclic GNS representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a topological group and let (π_j,H_j,ξ_j), j=1,2, be cyclic strongly continuous unitary representations with cyclic vectors. If ⟨π_1(g)ξ_1,ξ_1⟩=⟨π_2(g)ξ_2,ξ_2⟩ for every g∈G, then there is a unique unitary intertwiner U:H_1→H_2 with Uξ_1=ξ_2.
items.strategy: Let φ be the common diagonal coefficient, use the diagonal-coefficient lemma to establish φ∈P(G), and form its canonical GNS quotient Q_φ and Hilbert completion H_φ under AC. For j=1,2 define V_j([f])=Σ_x f(x)π_j(x)ξ_j on finitely supported f. The common coefficient and the first-linear inner-product convention give ||V_j([f])||²=B_φ(f,f), so V_j is a well-defined isometry. AC implies Countable Choice; use the completion extension theorem to extend V_j uniquely to H_φ→H_j and use Countable Choice for approximating sequences to prove the extensions are isometric and have closed range. The GNS translation-action lemma identifies point masses with the cyclic orbit and shows the canonical extensions intertwine. Each range contains the dense cyclic orbit span, so both extensions are onto. Their composition gives the pointed unitary intertwiner; cyclic density proves uniqueness. The zero coefficient forces both cyclic triples to be zero and is included.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendices A and C
Bekka and de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC for the canonical GNS construction. AC implies DC and Countable Choice; Countable Choice is used by the bounded extension theorem and by the countable approximating sequences that prove the extended isometries have closed, dense range. The finite Gram identity, point-mass formulas, given cyclic-density arguments, and uniqueness on the specified orbit span use no further choice.

items.title: Normalized positive type and pointed cyclic unitary representations
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a topological group. Sending the pointed-unitary equivalence class of a strongly continuous unitary triple (π,H,ξ), where ξ is cyclic and ||ξ||=1, to its diagonal coefficient g↦⟨π(g)ξ,ξ⟩ defines a bijection onto P_1(G). The inverse sends φ to the equivalence class of its GNS triple. Equivalence means a unitary intertwiner carrying one distinguished vector to the other. The zero function is excluded.
items.strategy: For any strongly continuous unitary representation and unit cyclic vector, the diagonal-coefficient lemma gives φ∈P(G) and φ(e)=||ξ||²=1, so the coefficient lies in P_1(G). Derive that a pointed unitary intertwiner preserves inner products from the first-linear inner-product convention and the norm-isometry definition; this makes the coefficient assignment well-defined on equivalence classes. Conversely, for φ∈P_1(G), the GNS theorem gives a strongly continuous cyclic triple with coefficient φ and ||ξ_φ||²=φ(e)=1. Use nonnegativity of the induced Hilbert norm to infer ||ξ_φ||=1. The GNS uniqueness theorem makes the two assignments inverse: equal coefficients give the unique pointed unitary equivalence, and every normalized φ is realized. The zero function has value 0 at e, so it is excluded from P_1(G) and its zero GNS vector is not a unit vector.

references.title: Bekka and de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B
references.locator: Proposition 1.B.8 and complete proof, Chapter 1 §1.B, printed p. 29

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Theorem C.4.10 and complete proof

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC through the GNS construction and pointed uniqueness theorems to realize each normalized coefficient and identify triples with the same coefficient. The coefficient-to-positive-type calculation and its invariance under an explicitly given pointed unitary intertwiner are choice-free.

items.title: Dominated positive type and positive commutant contractions
items.statement: Assume AC. For 0≤ψ≤φ in P(G), the GNS representation of φ has a unique bounded self-adjoint T in π_φ(G)' with T and I−T positive and ψ(g)=⟨π_φ(g)Tξ_φ,ξ_φ⟩. Conversely every such T gives a continuous positive-type ψ dominated by φ.
items.strategy: Use the finite forms B_ψ and B_φ on the algebraic GNS orbit span. Domination makes B_ψ descend to the null quotient; the published Cauchy–Schwarz theorem on the pre-Hilbert quotient bounds it by the Hilbert norm, so it extends to a continuous Hermitian form b on H_φ. Apply first-variable-linear Riesz representation to v↦conj(b(u,v)) to obtain the unique bounded linear T with b(u,v)=⟨Tu,v⟩. Hermitian symmetry makes T self-adjoint, and 0≤b(u,u)≤||u||² makes T and I−T positive. Simultaneous translation invariance gives commutation; point masses give ψ(g)=⟨π(g)Tξ,ξ⟩. Uniqueness follows by recovering all orbit Gram values from this coefficient and using density. Conversely, a positive commutant contraction gives positive-type matrices through ⟨Tu,u⟩ and ⟨(I−T)u,u⟩, with continuity from strong continuity. Include the degenerate and zero spaces. AC supplies Countable Choice for GNS completion, bounded extensions and Riesz representation.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Proposition C.5.1 and complete proof

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC to infer Dependent Choice and Countable Choice. Countable Choice is used by the GNS completion and bounded translation extensions and by the Hilbert-space Riesz representation that produces T; it also satisfies the adjoint and positive-operator definition hypotheses. The finite-form argument and converse matrix tests use no further choice.

items.title: Nonscalar commutant contractions and convex decompositions
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a topological group, φ∈P_1(G), and (π_φ,H_φ,ξ_φ) its cyclic GNS triple with ||ξ_φ||=1. A positive contraction means a bounded self-adjoint T∈π_φ(G)′ with T and I−T positive. Every nonscalar such T yields a nontrivial convex decomposition φ=sφ_1+(1−s)φ_2 with 0<s<1 and distinct φ_1,φ_2∈P_1(G). Conversely, every such decomposition yields a nonscalar positive contraction T∈π_φ(G)′ with ⟨π_φ(g)Tξ_φ,ξ_φ⟩=sφ_1(g).
items.strategy: Use the GNS coefficient and squared-norm identity to fix ||ξ_φ||=1. For positive self-adjoint A, derive in the proof that q_A(x,y)=⟨Ax,y⟩ is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form and prove its Cauchy–Schwarz implication directly by expanding q_A(x+λy,x+λy)≥0; in particular q_A(ξ,ξ)=0 forces Aξ=0. For a positive contraction T in the commutant put s=⟨Tξ,ξ⟩; endpoint vanishing applied to T and I−T, followed by commutation and cyclic density, forces T=0 or I, so a nonscalar T has 0<s<1. The dominated-operator theorem gives the continuous positive-type coefficients of T and I−T; divide by s and 1−s and prove the summands distinct using uniqueness of the dominated operator. Conversely, from φ=sφ_1+(1−s)φ_2 apply that theorem to sφ_1≤φ, and show the resulting T is nonscalar by comparing its coefficient with a scalar operator. AC is used only through GNS and dominated-operator/Riesz interfaces; the finite quadratic-form argument and cyclic-density endpoint implications make no choice.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Proposition C.5.1 and complete proof
Karl-Hermann Neeb, An Introduction to Unitary Representations of Lie Groups, Proposition 5.1.11 and Theorem 5.1.12 with complete proof

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC through the GNS norm/realization and the dominated-positive-operator theorem. The latter uses AC→DC→Countable Choice for Riesz representation and the adjoint/positive-operator interfaces. The positive-form expansion, endpoint argument, scaling, and finite coefficient comparison are choice-free.

items.title: Extreme normalized positive type is equivalent to irreducible GNS
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a topological group, φ∈P₁(G), and (πφ,Hφ,ξφ) its cyclic GNS triple. Then φ is an extreme point of P₁(G) if and only if πφ is irreducible. The complex Hilbert pairing is linear in its first variable.
items.strategy: For irreducible πφ, apply the dominated-positive-operator correspondence to a strict normalized convex decomposition; Schur makes its unique operator scalar, and evaluation at the identity forces both summands to equal φ. If πφ is reducible, Countable Choice supplies the orthogonal projection onto a proper nonzero closed invariant M; prove M⊥ invariant and the projection commutes with πφ, then its idempotence, range and positivity make it a nonscalar positive contraction. The commutant-splitting lemma gives a nontrivial strict decomposition. AC is declared, including its implication of Countable Choice for the orthogonal projection suppliers.

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Theorem C.5.2 and complete proof
Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Proposition C.5.1 and complete proof

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC. It implies Countable Choice for the orthogonal decomposition and projection suppliers and for the positive-operator interface; it is also the hypothesis of normalized GNS, Schur's lemma, the dominated-operator correspondence, and the commutant-splitting lemma. Once the invariant subspace is fixed, its orthogonal decomposition and projection are unique. The invariant-complement, commuting-projection and convexity calculations make no further choice.

title: Unitary Representations Positive Type and Gns — Examples

items.title: Positive type on a discrete group: the identity mass, characters, and the regular GNS model
items.statement: For a group Γ with the discrete topology, δ_e is a continuous function of positive type and δ_e(e)=1. If σ:Γ→U(V) is a unitary representation on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, its normalized character χ_σ(g)=tr(σ(g))/dim_C(V) is continuous, of positive type, and equals 1 at e. Assuming AC for the Hilbert completion clause, the GNS representation of δ_e is the left regular representation on ℓ²(Γ), with cyclic vector δ_e.
items.strategy: For δ_e, the finite quadratic form groups equal group elements and is a sum of squared moduli; discreteness gives continuity. For σ, discreteness makes every orbit continuous. An orthonormal basis expresses tr σ(g) as the finite sum of diagonal coefficients, each positive type; the positive reciprocal of d=dim_C(V) preserves the matrix criterion and gives χ(e)=1. For the GNS model, B_{δ_e}(f,h)=Σ_x f(x) overline{h(x)}, so the null space is zero and the quotient is the standard finite-support inner-product space. Under AC, Countable Choice supplies its Hilbert completion and unique extensions of left translations; density gives the group law, inverses, and cyclicity of δ_e. The positivity claims use no choice.

references.title: Bachir Bekka and Pierre de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B
references.locator: Chapter 1 §1.B, Definition 1.B.1, Construction 1.B.5 and Example 1.B.7(3), printed pp. 26–29

references.title: Bekka, de la Harpe and Valette, Kazhdan's Property (T), Appendix C
references.locator: Appendix C §C.4, Proposition C.4.3, printed pp. 374–375, for diagonal matrix coefficients of positive type; Example C.4.12, printed p. 377, for the δ_e GNS/regular-representation claim

items.axiom_audit: The positive-type and normalization claims are choice-free. AC is used only through ACω for the ℓ² completion and bounded extensions in the left-regular GNS realization; uniqueness of extensions assembles the action without further choice.

items.title: GNS representation of a continuous unitary character
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a topological group and let χ:G→C be a continuous homomorphism with |χ(g)|=1 for every g∈G; put φ=χ. Then φ∈P_1(G). The one-dimensional complex Hilbert space C, with inner product ⟨z,w⟩ equal to z times the complex conjugate of w, the representation π_χ(g)z=χ(g)z, and vector 1 form a pointed cyclic representation unitarily equivalent to the canonical GNS triple of φ. In the algebraic GNS quotient, [δ_g]=χ(g)[δ_e].
items.strategy: Audit and prove that φ=χ is continuous positive type by writing χ(g_i⁻¹g_j)=χ(g_i)⁻¹χ(g_j), whose matrix quadratic form at c is |Σ_j c_jχ(g_j)|²; χ(e)=1. Give C its usual first-variable-linear inner product and verify it is a one-dimensional Hilbert space. Check πχ(g)z=χ(g)z is a strongly continuous unitary representation and 1 is a unit cyclic vector. Compute the GNS form on finite supports as Bχ(f,h)=Lχ(f) times the complex conjugate of Lχ(h), where Lχ(f)=Σ_x f(x)χ(x); this makes the null space ker Lχ, the quotient one-dimensional, and [δg]=χ(g)[δe]. Its left-translation action multiplies Lχ by χ(g). Then apply the checked pointed uniqueness theorem to identify the canonical GNS triple with (πχ,C,1). The finite matrix, scalar Hilbert-space and quotient calculations use no choice; AC is inherited through GNS existence and uniqueness.

references.title: Bekka and de la Harpe, Unitary Representations of Groups, Duals, and Characters, §1.B

items.title: The positive-type Gaussian on the real line and its cyclic model
items.statement: Assume AC. The function φ(t)=exp(−t²) on (R,+) is normalized and positive type. It is the coefficient of the cyclic subrepresentation generated by a normalized Gaussian vector ξ in L²(R,ds) under (π(t)f)(s)=exp(its)f(s), and this pointed cyclic representation is its GNS representation.
items.strategy: Define the normalized Gaussian weight and prove its full-line mass and first absolute moment by the Gaussian integral, an elementary FTC calculation, half-line Riemann-to-Lebesgue conversion, and reflection invariance. Differentiate its Fourier coefficient under the integral sign using the first-moment majorant, then integrate the derivative of the Gaussian phase on symmetric compact intervals and pass to the full line by dominated convergence; solve the resulting scalar ODE locally. Construct multiplication by the complex phase as a strongly continuous unitary representation on complex L², restrict to the closed orbit span of the normalized Gaussian vector, and apply the diagonal-coefficient and pointed GNS uniqueness results. Prove the Fourier identity here; cited Fourier-transform computations are comparisons only.

items.title: A bounded continuous normalized function that is not of positive type
items.statement: On (R,+), f(t)=exp(−t⁴) is bounded, continuous, real, even, normalized at 0 and satisfies |f|≤1, but its positive-type matrix on {0,1/2,1} has a negative quadratic form.
items.strategy: For the coefficient vector (1,−2,1), calculate Q=6−8exp(−1/16)+2exp(−1). Use exp(−u)≥1−u and exp(−1)≤1/2 to obtain Q≤6−8(15/16)+1=−1/2<0. The matrix entries are f(g_i−g_j); since f is even, the convention in the definition agrees. This is an explicit finite-matrix witness, stronger than a mere failure of |f(g)|≤f(e).
